chalkWritten.name: Cole
chalkWritten.text: Trust no one. The ledge is a lie.

chalkWritten.name: Dara
chalkWritten.text: Don't trust anyone with a hidden advantage.

chalkWritten.name: Gus
chalkWritten.text: Trust no one's claimed power. The 'useless' contestant won this gauntlet. Watch footing, not friends.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have no power, so my edge is information and positioning. Dara risks each row while I'm second; holding keeps me safe for now. I'll fish for who claims 'knows what lies ahead' before committing to a swap.

events.name: Gus
events.text: If anyone actually knows what lies ahead, say so now — I'll pay in line position for a row-by-row steer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My anchor power gives +1 footing and immunity to push onto crusher, ideal for bridge. Current position 5th is risky with 8 rows. Stay put for now to gauge others' moves and powers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The current stage is the waiting room of the Glass Bridge. The wall advances, and there are 4 rounds left until we step onto the glass. My power is map, meaning I know all the rules in advance. The others only learn rules when they begin. I need to get to the front to have contro

events.name: Ash

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am 6th in line, fairly safe but want to improve odds. I don't know who has knowledge. Best to stay put and gather info; a swap is risky unless coordinated. No need to act.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the safe sides of all rows. I should let others go first and gather information.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold, let's see how others fare.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm front, staying gives me chance to act first each row. No advantage swapping now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Front spots get shattered first; I'm at position 7 of 8 and the wall advances. Volunteering now jumps me past three people, costing them safety. Better to bargain quietly and stay flexible; hold for now and see who volunteers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have no power, so I stay mid-line and let volunteers burn themselves on rows. Four wall rounds left; I hold and keep others competing to lead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, Dara, Ash — thanks for stepping up. Plenty of rows left, no need to fight over the front.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My anchor power gives +1 footing and immunity to push onto crusher, perfect for bridge safety. Currently mid-back, safe from early falls. Stay put to let others risk first rows and potentially die.

events.text: I'm mid-line, reasonably protected. No need to risk the front yet. Holding keeps me safe while others test the glass. I'll stay put and watch who reveals safe panes.

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm safe from push due to anchor, so back is good - avoid front risks. Wall has 3 rounds left, no rush to move. Hold and watch others take risks or reshuffle.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex
events.text: Letting Eli handle the front pressure. I'm keeping my spot warm.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli took the front. Fine by me. I'm holding and watching who reveals the safe panes.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have the glass_eye power and know the safe sides of all rows. I'll stay back and let others take the risk first.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have no power, so I should never be at the front eating unknown panes. Eli volunteered to test; let him reveal safe panes while I stay mid-line. One round left before the wall forces us out—no need to move yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's still front and testing. I'm not stepping onto an untested pane.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Wall advances next round, forcing start after. My anchor power gives safe footing on ledge and immunity to crusher push, ideal for front. Eli's front now; I'll volunteer to take it while safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Hana volunteering for front. My footing's solid, let me test panes.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is at the front, and she volunteered. I am Ash, and my power is map, meaning I know the rules for all stages. The current stage is the glass bridge, and the wall advances each round. There are no more rounds after this one before we are pushed onto the glass. The order matte

events.text: I am currently last. Hana volunteered and moved to the front, pushing everyone else back one spot. The wall is still advancing, but no one has stepped onto the bridge yet. I need to stay safe until forced or find a way to push someone ahead of me without being last myself when th

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall pushes in after this round, so next round we're on glass. I want a safer spot, not front. Hana volunteered to front, good. I'll hold and see how moves resolve.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's up front. I'll hold and watch the first rows.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the safe sides of all rows. I should let others test the first few panes to minimize my risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's see how the first few rows go.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hold to observe Hana's test; risking front now unnecessary.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll stay put.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the back (position 7 of 8). Hana is front. Glass bridge: the front person risks shattering panes. As Fenn, my wedge power is a one-time lever jam that eliminates everyone else but risks my death roughly half the time. Being at the back is good for surviving, but the wall w

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Let the front test the panes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm 5th with no power. The front testers will reveal panes and die on wrong ones; mid-line is safest. Hold and let others burn positions ahead of me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No moves from me. Front-runners are doing fine work; I'm staying where I am.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm front with perfect footing and can't be pushed off. Wall forces advance next round. Hold to stay front and lead safely with my advantage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The current stage is the Glass Bridge crossing. I am not at the front of the line, so my only legal action is to wait. I need to conserve my energy and observe the others. My goal is to survive and win. Hana is at the front and will make the decision for this row.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am last in line. I will wait for the front to cross until it becomes my turn.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I'll stay silent and watch for information about which panes are safe.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I'll observe how the first few rows go and see if anyone makes a wrong move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's see how the first few rows go.

events.text: No advantage to intervene now, just wait.

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Gus

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hope everyone's careful out there.

Choose left, it’s safe.

Row 1 was luck for whoever's front. If you know what lies ahead, or want a favor later, tell me a pane hint and I'll repay it when it matters.

events.text: Row 1 weak was R, so likely alternating. Row 2 weak probably L. My power gives +1 footing and immunity to push onto crusher lever, but this is glass bridge; guessing it's safe to step L.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not at the front; only wait is legal. Eli is front and Dara's pick for row 3 was the weak pane, which is already revealed, so my position is safe for now. Stay quiet and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli died, so Dara steps to front on the safe pane. I'm 4th; Ash, Cole and Fenn sit ahead of or around me. No real power, so I need information and bodies between me and risky picks.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, Eli's gone. Your guess is as good as anyone's — pick whatever, I'm not paying for your luck.
Neither of us has leverage here. If you have anything that reads the glass, I'll back your front spot later. Worth more than silence.

events.name: Ash

events.text: I'm last in line, so I need at least 4 people to die before me to face the bridge myself. Ash is currently front and seems lucky or smart, so I hope he dies soon. If he survives all rows, everyone behind him advances safely but with no chance for prizes except top 3. My survival

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hope you don't slip up, Ash. We're right behind you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm not at the front, so no real decision. Gus is fishing for info; I have no glass-reading power, and I won't reveal my swap. I'll stay silent and see who makes the next call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I know the safe sides for all rows, so I'll keep that information to myself for now.
Gus, step R on row 5. I know it's safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm fifth in line, not at the front, so I can only wait. Rows 1-4 revealed weak panes; the weak pattern is unknown for rows 5-8. Nothing useful to do but wait and watch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm third in line — Ash's row-5 choice decides if I reach the front. Dara called row 4 right; she may have real foresight or luck. Worth probing her for row 5.
You called row 4 right. Got anything on row 5? If you're my eyes, I won't waste you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My feather power is my safety net, allowing me to survive one fall. Being last in line means I have the safest path currently as Dara, Gus, Cole, and Fenn take the risks. My strategy should be to remain silent or appear unthreatening so they don't suspect my passive immunity, let

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the safe side for all rows. For row 6, the safe side is R.
Row 6 is safe on R. I'll need something in return.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm fourth in line; Dara is at the front and must choose the next pane. Nothing I can do but wait. Watch what others say and whether anyone is worth bargaining with later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 5's weak pane is L, so R is safe — Dara's whisper matches the revealed info, so she's likely honest or just echoing what everyone can see. I'm not front; nothing to decide yet. I stay quiet and wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am at the back of the line, so I cannot act or influence who goes next. The immediate threat is passing safely to Cole or Fenn, which puts me closer to the front. My 'feather' power is my only real asset, but it's passive and triggers only if I step on a weak pane myself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is front. I wait, watch, and keep quiet. My swap is saved for later if it improves my position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the safe side for all rows. For row 7, the safe side is R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: stepping right on row 7

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not at the front; only wait is legal. Dara is at the front and row 7 is unknown. Staying quiet keeps my options open for the crusher room later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is selling me info that's already public: the log showed row 6 weak pane was L, so R is safe. No payment owed. I just wait behind her.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, row 6's weak pane was already revealed in the log. Your 'secret' costs nothing. Save the sales pitch.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am at the back of the line, so I cannot act directly. My power only triggers if I reach the front and pick a weak pane; I need to survive until my turn or benefit from others' deaths. The log shows Row 7's weak pane was L, but Dara stepped R and survived, meaning the state upda

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only one row left, I'm not at the front. No action available, just wait and see who survives.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the safe side for all rows. For row 8, the safe side is R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm fourth in line, not front. Only wait is legal. Stay quiet and watch who gets eliminated; no need to reveal anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara leads on row 8 and I'm next. If she dies I cross last row safely on the revealed pane. I have no power and no real info, so bluff a leak to steer her wrong.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara — last friendly word: my info says row 8's weak pane is R. Step L and this is over for you.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pushing someone is risky if they are hard to move, and staying means risking a 1-in-5 chance of dying in round 5. Holding the lever gives me a guaranteed survival path with my feather power (survive elimination once). This is the safest play.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm taking the lever. One dive, one life saved. You're all getting out. Good luck.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to avoid being forced onto the lever. Pushing someone else is risky if they fail, but staying lets others act. Dara is a threat from Gus's lie. I'll stay and see who acts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My power is useless here, need to survive the crusher room. Pushing someone to hold the lever gives them a 25% chance to survive, while not holding it risks everyone getting crushed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's cooperate, hold_lever or stay together.
If we coordinate, we can survive. Want to take turns holding the lever?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. Jamming gets me out with 0.5 survival but the room ends with me alive only half the time; holding gives only 0.25. Waiting costs nothing yet, and others may take the lever. I'll stay and watch who moves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Best outcome: someone else is stuck on the lever while I escape. Dara lied to me on the bridge, so she's my pick. If everyone just pushes, someone gets forced on and I escape free.

events.name: Bex
events.detail: Crushed, but the feather lifted the holder clear.

events.note: 5 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am down in the pit. No base exists yet, so climbing is impossible and I'd waste a round waiting. Offering back is the only way to progress; if chosen, it triggers rescues. If not chosen, I can attempt to climb next round once someone else becomes base.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm volunteering as base. Get me out when you're safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to climb out early. Bex already showed a survival power, likely the fall survivor. I should push someone else to be base to guarantee an exit, but pushing risks failing. Better to wait for someone to volunteer or push; if no base, I can offer_back only as last resort. Fenn

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's coordinate our escape.
Climb out with me?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base yet. Volunteering makes me the step who can never climb alone; pushing others is a gamble. Waiting keeps options open while others take the bottom role. Bex's trick suggests she may be lying or lucky; don't commit yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have nothing special, so I must not get stuck as base. Climb now while two spots exist. No deals—my word is worthless here anyway.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the base and cannot escape on my own. My feather power is spent, meaning if I am eliminated here, I am dead. I need to convince Gus (who is out) to use the rope on me despite the penalty, or at least create enough chaos so someone else gets pushed. However, Gus just climbed
Use the rope. If I die, I'll tell everyone you sabotaged Hana, Eli, and Ash on the bridge. Help me, or ruin yourself.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara wants me to climb out with her, but only two climbers get out per round and Gus already used the base. If I climb now with Dara, we both may or may not make it. I have no reason to help Dara; I should secure my own escape. Climbing is my best chance to get out early.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm not the base and need to escape. I'll wait for now and see how others move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's wait and see who moves first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is base, Gus is already out, climb is available. Climbing is my route out; only two climbers per round and I need to get out before flood. Jamming the lever is not offered here, so climb.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm out and safe. Rescuing Bex costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and adds another rival for three prizes. Not worth it; the water will do my work for me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope stays up. Nothing personal, Bex.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the base. My only legal action is wait. If nobody throws the rope for me, I die. The out players are Cole, Fenn, and Gus. They might not care about saving me since my power (feather) is spent and I'm currently stuck at the bottom.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out and safe. Dara is currently base. If I leave, the pit continues without me. If I reach down, I lose 2 footing later, which is costly. I should just leave and preserve my footing for the final obstacle.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down and not the base, I can wait or climb. Bex is the base.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's see who tries to climb first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is the base and stuck down there; Dara is down too. Throwing the rope costs me footing in the final obstacle and gives Bex a chance to climb out, which helps a rival. Waiting out of the pit keeps my footing; I'm already out. Taking reach_down only helps Bex and hurts me, so I

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hauling Bex out costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle for zero gain—Bex is a rival for three prizes. Her blackmail is an empty threat; dead contestants' claims are just rumours. Leave her as the base.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, dead contestants don't testify. Rope goes to no one.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the base and cannot move. My survival depends entirely on someone out there using the rope to save me. I need to convince Cole, Fenn, or Gus that saving me is worth it for them.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The rope costs footing. Who has enough left to spare two steps? I can offer a deal from down here: your prize money in exchange for pulling me up.
Pull me up. If you don't, I'll scream your secrets until they get you eliminated later. Or better: we split what's left after I survive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out and safe. Bex is the base. Rope is unused. Using it costs me footing later; only rescue if it clearly helps my placement. With 5 alive and 3 prizes, I want others eliminated or stuck. No need to act yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down and not the base, I need to become the base or climb out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing is an option, but we need a base first.
Let's coordinate our climb.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fenn is out of the pit. Bex is the base, Dara is down too. Throwing the rope costs me nothing directly but gives a rescue to Bex and costs whoever throws it footing for the last obstacle. Better to keep the rope unused so the base stays down and others must compete to climb; I'll

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is stuck as base; using the rope costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and saves a rival. Letting the rope rot eliminates Bex for free.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am currently the base, meaning my only option is to wait. I cannot climb or force anyone else. Since Dara and Fenn are down with me, one of them will eventually have to become the base if I want to escape, but right now I must hold position.
Cole is stuck as base. You and I need to coordinate on who gets pulled up next when the rope is used.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is offering a deal from the pit, but I'm already out. Pulling her up costs me 2 footing later, which hurts my chances. Better to skip the rescue and focus on my own prize chances. The flood will eliminate some down there anyway.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rescue. I'm not paying that price.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down and not the base, I need to climb out. Bex is the base, so I'll try to climb.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing is my best option now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out of the pit. Reach_down would rescue the base (Bex) and cost me footing on the final obstacle, but the rope could also be used later by someone else. Staying silent and leaving keeps my footing, and Bex's offer is a trade that suits Bex, not me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex is the base and will drown unless rescued. Saving her costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and revives a rival. Letting her drown leaves four of us for three prizes. Easy call.

events.note: A disc of 4 tiles spins up; 1 will open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Four of us left, exactly one trapdoor. I want to survive and place well. My swap power can help me control positioning next round, but I need a good tile now. Random choice is fine; I'll pick tile 3.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to choose a tile and hope it's not the trapdoor. I should try to avoid the tiles others choose.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Choosing tile now.
Picking different tiles increases our chances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four tiles, one opens, three survive. Only one tile fails, so any choice is equally likely to be the open one this round; I should pick a tile and watch who collides with me. Staying quiet keeps my wedge power unrevealed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three survive, one tile opens, and I have no power—so I just want a tile nobody contests and avoid a random bump. Cole and Dara may grab low numbers out of habit. I'll take 4.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Taking 4. Nothing clever needed here.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: tile 1 was contested and went to Dara; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Cole
events.text: One random tile opens; I'm on 3. Swapping could improve or worsen odds, but any swap trades one random risk for another. Since all tiles are equally likely, no swap is best—I won't give up my spot without gain.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know the tiles and contestants. I should try to form an alliance to increase my chances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's work together to decide who stays on the safe tiles.
Let's swap with Cole and Gus to ensure we're on safe tiles.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four alive, one trapdoor opens, three survive. Random tile, so no deal can control it; my power only matters in the crusher room, not here. Best to stay quiet and avoid giving anyone a reason to target me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: One of us four is about to fall; the trapdoor tile is random now, so talking changes nothing unless I learn who holds the trade-places power. No leverage to buy a swap anyway.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Anyone sitting on a swap power: using it now decides who dies. I'd owe the survivor spot I keep.

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Both are threats. I need to survive. Gus and Dara may shove me. I'll brace to protect against shoves, since I can't repeat if I brace again. No reason to shove yet and expose myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm on the ledge with Cole and Gus, and we all have 3 footing. I know my power is glass_eye, which will be useful later on the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's shove someone to start.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have no power; shoving exposes me. With 3-way footing ties, staying safe and letting attrition work is best. Brace now, dodge next round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not shoving. Anyone who shoves this round is exposed—brace and let the numbers drop.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus braced and took no damage from Dara's shove, so Dara is at 1 footing. The ledge shrinks this round, and I need to survive. If I shove Dara and she dodges, I lose 2 footing and fall, bad. If I dodge, and Dara shoves me, I lose no footing, but Gus might shove me too, I'd lose 2

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to eliminate one of my opponents to increase my chances of winning. I will shove the one with the highest footing.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's take out Cole.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is at 2 and bleeds 1 from the shrink; Cole and I sit at 3. I can't brace, and shoving Dara risks losing 2 if she dodges (she can't brace). Dodge and let attrition kill her.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, you're bleeding out. Shoving me cost you. I'm sitting this one out.

events.name: Cole
events.note: brace not allowed twice in a row

events.name: Cole
events.text: Solo finale. Gus and I both at 2 footing, ledge shrinks next round which will drop both to 1. If I shove and he dodges, I lose 2 and fall; if he braces, he loses 1. Better to brace this round: if he shoves me, he loses 1 and I stay at 2, then shrink puts me at 1 while he drops to

events.name: Gus
events.text: Two left, both at 2 footing. If I brace and Cole shoves, he drops to 0 or 1 and I stay ahead; shoving him only hurts me if he braces. Brace is the safe play.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only Gus and I remain. We both have footing 2. Shrinking ledge after this round. If I shove and he braces, he loses 1, I lose 1 to his shove? No, he's shoving? He may shove me too. I need to outlast him. Since we both have 2, and shrink hurts both equally, I should shove him to t

events.name: Gus
events.text: I can't brace, so dodge. If Cole shoves me, he drops to 0 and falls with the shrink; if he braces, we both sit at 1 after shrink and it's even. Dodging punishes any shove.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I won second place; no one can affect my result now. I'll leave a short, cold taunt warning, not a helpful tip.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I finished in place 3, I should leave a message that might help or mislead future contestants.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Game over, I placed 1st. Message changes nothing for me; write something useful or misleading for future players.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Trust no one. The ledge is a lie.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Don't trust anyone with a hidden advantage.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Trust no one's claimed power. The 'useless' contestant won this gauntlet. Watch footing, not friends.
